title: SSE subscription leasing, chunk sequence monotonicity, and prioritized reconnect logic
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Customers rely on long-lived SSE connections for streaming model outputs (tokens, tool calls, structured fragments). Current reconnect behavior can lose small tail fragments or cause duplicate function-call frames when clients retry aggressively. This ticket defines a subscription-lease model with compact checkpoint tokens, monotonic chunk sequencing, and a prioritized reconnect strategy to enable near-lossless client replay while bounding server memory and retention costs.

Goals and scope:
- Define compact, forward-compatible lease token that encodes subscription id, last-seen seq, and server retention epoch.
- Ensure chunk monotonicity across reconnects (client can request replay from seq+1) and enforce idempotency for function-call/structured frames.
- Implement prioritized reconnect/backoff: short immediate probe for transient network flaps, then exponential backoff with capped tail-replay window; allow higher-tier customers shorter retention and faster probes.
- Minimal server-side retention: cooperative eviction policy with explicit lease renewal path.
- Small SDK changes to surface checkpoints and automatic resume; provide opt-in strict-ordered semantics for apps that require exact-at-most-once function-call handling.

Design decisions / trade-offs:
- Checkpoint token format chosen as base62(token_prefix|seq|epoch|sig) to keep overhead small in headers; avoids heavy JWT parsing on servers. Trade-off: less human-readable, easier to evolve.
- Server will keep per-subscription rolling window of last N chunks (configurable per plan). We accept potential partial replay beyond retention -> clients must be prepared for gap errors. This bounds memory and retention costs.
- Strict at-most-once across reconnects requires server-side idempotency mapping of function-call IDs for retention window; increases memory but gated behind a per-subscription flag. Default is at-least-once for tokens to prioritize throughput.
- Prioritized reconnect behavior: SDK issues a 300ms probe with Authorization+Lease token; if no response, it escalates to jittered exponential backoff. Private/Dedicated tenants may configure probe durations.

API/Protocol notes:
- New SSE initialization flow: client GET /stream?subscription_id=... header: Authorization, X-Redwood-Lease: <lease-token>
- Server response includes: initial comment with server-lease: <lease-token>, retention-epoch header, and initial seq baseline.
- Chunk framing: each event uses event: chunk
  data: {"seq": 12345, "type": "delta|call|structured", "id": "<opaque>", "payload": "..."}
- Client resume: if reconnecting, client supplies last-seen seq in X-Redwood-Resume-Seq or the lease token. Server validates epoch and either serves replay from seq+1 or returns 412 with gap indication if seq older than retention.

Acceptance criteria (prod-ready):
- Server emits server-lease header and maintains per-subscription rolling buffer configurable by plan.
- SDK (node/python) automatically emits a 300ms probe on small disconnects and resumes using lease+seq.
- Function-call frames include idempotency id and server honors idempotent mapping during retention window when strict-ordered mode enabled.
- Comprehensive unit + integration tests covering: short-flap reconnect, gap error path, probe success path, idempotent replay dedupe.

Migration plan:
1. Deploy server-side support behind feature-flag.
2. Roll out SDK changes as opt-in in patch releases.
3. Flip default probe behavior for hosted customers after 2-week dogfood.

Open questions:
- Retention sizing: default N=500 chunks vs latency trade-offs for high-throughput customers. (Perf team to benchmark.)
- How to surface replay gap errors in Console: quick link to a per-subscription replay window visualization?
